answer: The relic lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the marble is where a second reviewer recomputes them. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The design leans on staked peer review with spot checks, diluted when peers disagree, no identity may audit its own recruit. The pulse of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce.
